title: Eight Winters and One Short Mark
subtitle: 体育赛事 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育赛事（人与社会·文学、艺术与体育）
meta: 主题语境：体育赛事（人与社会·文学、艺术与体育）　|　核心词汇：entry　|　正文 348 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 entry 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 my father ① made an entry that no clerk in the office would have read, and he said the making was the whole of the winter. The ② entry, meaning the line itself and not the page, ran eight winters and stayed unread in the book; an entry, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unread.

Every ③ entry in that office had the same short mark beside it, and the ④ entry at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the race and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An entry, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to read; my father said the reading is the part that fills eight winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the entry was the whole of the competition, meaning the coming in and not the line. The ⑥ entry, meaning the coming in and not any of that, is the only thing in a competition that everybody waits for and nobody reads; entry, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a line and a coming in. He said the coming in is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ entry had become a line in a register, and the register had become an argument about the short mark. The ⑧ entry of the whole thing, my father wrote in January, was one office and eight winters of reading; entry, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to read. He said the reading was never mentioned.

The ⑨ entry I remember is the one read in the register, which closed in 1974 and is still described as the quietest in the office. An ⑩ entry, my mother said in 1976, is the only one that improves by being read; every entry, she said, is a coming in that has agreed to look like a line. She said the coming in was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 条目；词条（指办公室里每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 条目（指那一条本身，与整页相对）
C. 固定搭配：make an entry 记入一条；登记
D. n. 条目（指留给赛程的那一条）
E. n. 参赛作品（抽象总称，指一次比赛的参赛事）
F. n. 条目（指名册上写到、被登记的那一条）
G. n. 进入；入场（指比赛里人人都等却无人登记的那样东西）

answers.why: make an entry 意为“记入一条、登记”，1965 年父亲记下了一条办公室里没有一位办事员肯读的条目。
entry 意为“条目”，指那一条本身而不是整页，它经过了八个冬天而在簿子上没有记号。
entry 意为“条目”，指办公室里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一个短短的记号。
entry 意为“条目”，指留给赛程的那一条，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
entry 意为“进入、入场”，指比赛里人人都等却无人登记的那样东西，叔叔说这次入场就是那场比赛的全部。
entry 意为“进入”，指人人都等却无人登记的那种许可而不是那一条，是比赛里人人都等、却无人登记的东西。
entry 意为“条目”，指名册上写到、被登记的那一条，到 1971 年这一条成了名册里的一行。
entry 意为“参赛作品”，父亲一月写道，整件事的参赛事是一间办公室和八个冬天的阅读。
entry 意为“条目”，我记得的是名册上登记的那一条，1974 年结束了，至今仍被说成办公室里最安静的一条。
entry 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，一条参赛作品是唯一会因为被好好阅读而变得更好的东西。
